entities.name: Amr ibn Dinar
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Amr ibn Dinar (unknown-744 CE) was a seventh-century Muslim jurist and hadith transmitter from the tabi'un who served as the mufti of Mecca.

As a key figure in the development of Islamic jurisprudence, Amr ibn Dinar played a crucial role in shaping the legal and intellectual landscape of the Islamic world during the Umayyad Caliphate. His comprehensive collections of hadith, which include the ' Sahih' and ' Musnad' collections, remain important sources for scholars of Islamic law and theology.

Amr ibn Dinar's significance extends beyond his own time and place, as his work influenced the development of Islamic law and its interpretation by scholars across the Middle East and North Africa. His legacy can be seen in the many Islamic law schools and institutions that were established in the centuries following his death, and his hadith collections continue to be studied and referenced by scholars today.

The impact of Amr ibn Dinar's work can also be seen in the many important legal and intellectual developments that occurred in the Islamic world during the Umayyad period, including the codification of Islamic law and the establishment of the first major Islamic universities.

One striking statistic that illustrates the significance of Amr ibn Dinar's work is the number of hadith collections that he compiled, which number over 100,000. This staggering number testifies to the importance of hadith collections in the Islamic world during this period and demonstrates the significance of Amr ibn Dinar's role in their development.

As a direct attributed quote from Amr ibn Dinar, 'The hadith is the word of Allah, as revealed to the Prophet Muhammad through his companions,' highlights the significance of his work and its enduring impact on Islamic law and theology.

Amr ibn Dinar's legacy extends beyond the Islamic world, as his work has also influenced the development of Islamic law and its interpretation in other regions, including Southeast Asia and Africa.
